Average day Relatively safer night

In detail

Hampshire Constabulary recorded 400 crimes inside this ward's official boundary over the 3 months to July 2026 — 8.3 per 1,000 residents, the 11th highest rate of Portsmouth's 14 wards. The daytime score here is driven by shoplifting (22), vehicle crime (9), drugs (5); the evening/night score by violent crime (51), anti social behaviour (14), public order (7). Rated against the average of the city's own wards, never against another city.

Frequently asked questions

Is Central Southsea safe?

Wandroz currently rates Central Southsea in Portsmouth as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Portsmouth during the day and relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Portsmouth at night. This rating is derived from Hampshire Constabulary street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats.

Is Central Southsea safe at night?

At night, Central Southsea is rated as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Portsmouth. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Central Southsea a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Central Southsea's day rating (roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Portsmouth) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. You can search accommodation already filtered to this specific area using the Booking.com link on this page.
